findings.passage: “I refuse to allow votes to be silenced because of signature variances,” Young said. “Our election officials do a fantastic job – but they are not trained handwriting experts. If two signatures don’t match up, the voter must be notified and allowed to affirm their signature.”
findings.note: Release on her plan for a bill that would let a voter whose mail ballot signature does not match be notified and affirm the signature. Related to proving identity on a mail ballot.
subjects: what happens to a voter whose ballot is questioned

findings.passage: “Signatures vary over time. And we should not allow something as mundane as this to disenfranchise voters who want to make their voice heard,” Young said.
findings.note: Release announcing a 2023-24 bill that would require county boards of election to notify voters when a ballot signature does not match the one on file, so they can affirm their identity.
subjects: what happens to a voter whose ballot is questioned

findings.passage: “As an elected official, it is my duty to continue the fight to eliminate voting barriers and ensure all voices are heard,” Young said.
findings.note: Same release; general statement about voting barriers, in the context of her election bill and the voter-ID bill H.B. 1300 that the release says was vetoed.
